candidates.computation_change_reason: Cross-reference to Element I, Section I, Table 1 identifies which pollutants have numeric concentration limits and which must be recorded; different readings of the pollutant list or the cross-reference could change which enforceable limits apply (A) and which monitoring/recordkeeping obligations attach (B).

candidates.exact_span: The annual whole sludge application rate for the sewage sludge that does not cause the annual pollutant loading rates in Table 4 to be exceeded.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Table 4 annual pollutant loading rates define enforceable numeric loading limits tied to application rate (A); whether and how this rate must be determined and retained affects applicable monitoring and recordkeeping duties (B).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall report annually on the DMR the following information:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Annual DMR reporting cadence governs when monitoring results must be submitted; interpreting this as the operative reporting frequency versus other referenced frequencies (e.g., monthly averages) could change which monitoring periods are required (B) and how absent or partial results are classified as documented no-data versus missing evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: List Pollutant Table 4 appropriate for permittee's land application practices.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which Table 4 pollutant set applies depends on land application practices; a different interpretation of 'appropriate' or of the permittee's practices could change applicable loading-rate limits (A) and which pollutants must be reported (B).

candidates.exact_span: The frequency of monitoring listed in Element 1, Section I.C. which applies to the permittee.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Monitoring frequency is incorporated by reference from Element 1, Section I.C.; resolving which frequency applies to the permittee changes whether monitoring was required in a given period (B) and whether a missing result reflects a non-required period or inadequate evidence (C).

TCLP is a pass/fail rather than ordinary numeric limit comparison (A); it is a distinct reporting/monitoring requirement (B); and absent or non-numeric TCLP evidence must be classified differently from missing numeric pollutant concentrations (C).

candidates.exact_span: The concentration (mg/Kg) in the sludge of each pollutant listed in Table 1 (defined as a monthly average) found in Element 1, Section I.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies numeric pollutant concentrations in mg/Kg as monthly averages for Table 1 parameters, establishing both the compliance comparison basis and limit type (A), the substance and averaging period of required reporting (B), and the expected evidence shape when results are absent or only partially reported relative to annual DMR cadence (C).

candidates.exact_span: Class A pathogen reduction Alternative used as listed in Section I.B.3.a. Alternatives describe how the pathogen reduction requirements are met.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Requires reporting of a specific pathogen-reduction alternative rather than a numeric concentration; interpretation of which alternative applies or whether alternative selection satisfies the obligation affects monitoring/reporting applicability (B) and how non-numeric or missing alternative documentation is categorized (C).

candidates.exact_span: Vector attraction reduction Alternative used as listed in Section I.B.4.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Requires reporting of the vector attraction reduction alternative used; which alternative is operative changes applicable reporting duties (B) and the semantics of missing or incomplete evidence for that non-numeric requirement (C).
